date: "2026-10-29"
---

Central Question: How do FEMA disaster relief claims associated with Hurricane Helene correspond to social vulnerability data for impacted counties in NC? 

Supporting Questions: 
-Which counties in NC sustained the most building damage based on FEMA claims? 
-How do the overall SVI scores compare for those 10 counties? 
-How do the percentile rankings for each SVI sub-theme compare for the top 10 counties?
-What is the correlation between overall SVI percentiles and building damage? 

Variables: 
buildingDamageAmount- (dollars) 
countyCode- (numeric code)
RPL_THEME1- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Socioeconomic Status theme summary  
RPL_THEME2- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Household Characteristics theme summary 
RPL_THEME3- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Racial and Ethnic Minority Status theme 
RPL_THEME4- (percentile) Percentile ranking for Housing Type/ Transportation theme 
RPL_THEMES- (percentile) Overall percentile ranking 
```{r setup}
#install.packages("here")
library(readr)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
#loading appropriate packages
setwd(here())
getwd() 
#setting the wroking directory
FEMA_SVI_data <- read_csv(here
("data/processed/master_FEMA_SVI_data.csv"))
```

```{r figure fema}
tencounties_highest_claims <- c(37021, 37111, 37089, 37011, 37023,37115, 37009, 
                       37161, 37087, 37189)

FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(countyCode),y = buildingDamageAmount,
             color = factor(countyCode))) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Building Damage Amount by Top 10 County Codes FEMA Claim",
    x = "FIPS County Code", y = "Building Damage Amount ($)",
    color = "County Code") + theme_classic() +
    scale_color_discrete(labels = c(                                             
      #allows me to assign name to each code in legend
    "37021 = Buncombe",
    "37111 = Mcdowell",
    "37089 = Henderson",
    "37011 = Avery",
    "37009 = Ashe",
    "37115 = Madison",
    "37023 = Burke",
    "37161 = Rutherford",
    "37087 = Haywood",
    "37189 = Watauga")) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2000000))
```

```{r figure svi total}
FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(COUNTY %in% SVI_tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  distinct(COUNTY, RPL_THEMES) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(COUNTY),
             y = RPL_THEMES,
             fill = factor(COUNTY))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Overall Social Vulnerability Rating of Top 10 Most Damaged Counties",
    x = "County",
    y = "Overall Social Vulnerability Index (0-1)",
    fill = "County"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      vjust = 1,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
   
    
```

```{r summary table}
#creating summary table
summary_table <- FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  group_by(countyCode, COUNTY, RPL_THEMES) %>% 
  summarize(total_building_damage = sum(buildingDamageAmount, na.rm = TRUE), 
            .groups = "drop_last") %>% 
  #adding the building damage amount per county 
  select(countyCode, COUNTY, total_building_damage, RPL_THEMES) %>%
  as_tibble()

#changing column names to be more informative  
colnames(summary_table) <- c("FIPS County Code", "County", "Building Damage Amount ($)", 
                             "Overall Social Vulnerabilty Index (0-1)")
#view table
summary_table
    
```

```{r per capita table}

#Adding column to dataframe that has net building payment amount per capita using estimated total population column 
FEMA_SVI_PER_CAPITA <- FEMA_SVI_data %>% mutate(ratio = netBuildingPaymentAmount/E_TOTPOP) %>% rename ("NetBuildingPaymentPerCapita" = "ratio")

```

```{r figure with net building payment amount}

tencounties_highest_claims <- c(37021, 37111, 37089, 37011, 37023,37115, 37009, 
                       37161, 37087, 37189)

#building damage top ten counties
FEMA_SVI_data %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(countyCode),y = netBuildingPaymentAmount,
             color = factor(countyCode))) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Building Damage Amount by Top 10 County Codes FEMA Claim",
    x = "FIPS County Code", y = "Building Damage Amount ($)",
    color = "County Code") + theme_classic() +
    scale_color_discrete(labels = c(                                             
      #allows me to assign name to each code in legend
    "37021 = Buncombe",
    "37111 = Mcdowell",
    "37089 = Henderson",
    "37011 = Avery",
    "37009 = Ashe",
    "37115 = Madison",
    "37023 = Burke",
    "37161 = Rutherford",
    "37087 = Haywood",
    "37189 = Watauga")) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 900000))

```
```{r summary table with all SVI variables}

#creating summary table 2 with net building payment amount, per capita building payment amount, and all SVI vulnerability indices 

summary_table_2 <- FEMA_SVI_PER_CAPITA %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  group_by(countyCode, COUNTY, RPL_THEMES, RPL_THEME1, RPL_THEME2, RPL_THEME3, RPL_THEME4) %>%  
  #adding the building payment amount per county and per capita ratio
  summarize(total_building_payment = sum(netBuildingPaymentAmount, na.rm = TRUE), 
            total_building_payment_per_capita = sum(netBuildingPaymentAmount, na.rm = 
                                                    TRUE)/first(E_TOTPOP), .groups =
                                                    "drop_last") %>% 
  select(countyCode, COUNTY, total_building_payment, total_building_payment_per_capita,
         RPL_THEMES, RPL_THEME1, RPL_THEME2, RPL_THEME3, RPL_THEME4) %>%
  as_tibble()

#changing column names to be more informative  
colnames(summary_table_2) <- c("FIPS County Code", "County", "Net Building Payment Amount
                               ($)", "Net Building Payment Amount per capita", "Overall
                               Social
                               Vulnerabilty Index (0-1)", "Socioeconomic Vulnerability
                               (0-1)",
                               "Household Characteristic Vulnerability (0-1)", "Racial/Ethnic
                               Minority Vulnerability (0-1)", "Housing Type/Transportation
                               Vulnerability")
#view table 2
summary_table_2
    
```

```{r per capita boxplot}
tencounties_highest_claims <- c(37021, 37111, 37089, 37011, 37023,37115, 37009, 
                       37161, 37087, 37189)

tencounties_highest_claims <- c(
  37021, 37111, 37089, 37011, 37023,
  37115, 37009, 37161, 37087, 37189
)

FEMA_SVI_PER_CAPITA %>%
  filter(countyCode %in% tencounties_highest_claims) %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = factor(countyCode),
    y = NetBuildingPaymentPerCapita,
    color = factor(countyCode)
  )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Net Building Payment Per Capita by County",
    x = "County",
    y = "FEMA Net Building Payment Amount Per Capita",
    color = "County Code"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      vjust = 1,
      hjust = 1
    ), 
    legend.position = "none", 
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(
    "37021" = "Buncombe",
    "37111" = "McDowell",
    "37089" = "Henderson",
    "37011" = "Avery",
    "37009" = "Ashe",
    "37115" = "Madison",
    "37023" = "Burke",
    "37161" = "Rutherford",
    "37087" = "Haywood",
    "37189" = "Watauga"
  )) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 30))
```
